name: Bayesian Inverse Problems
summary: Infer a posterior distribution for unknown physical parameters from noisy observations.
core_idea: Combine prior distributions and an observation likelihood, then compute or approximate p(theta | y).
innovation: Quantifies parameter uncertainty, multimodality and prior assumptions rather than producing one fit alone.
limitations: Computing posterior distributions may require many costly forward evaluations.
Priors and likelihoods can strongly influence weakly identifiable parameters.

start_here.why: Influential unifying treatment of Bayesian inverse-problem formulation and well-posedness.
start_here.focus: Read the Bayesian formulation and computational overview first, not every proof.

curation_note: Core method concept and checked source(s) recorded; suggested readings remain advisory and may be revised.
